title: Perfect complexes are dualizable
statement: Let $p$ and $\ell$ be distinct primes, let $a,n\geq1$ be integers, put $q=p^a$, let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] on finite-type $k$-schemes and separated finite-type morphisms, and let $X$ be a scheme in that datum. Use its category $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and the coefficient unit $\Lambda_X$, derived tensor and derived internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus the integral unit is the completed coefficient sheaf and the field stages use scalar localization and the common finite-stage category, respectively. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be quasi-isomorphic, locally on the coefficient site of $X$, to a bounded complex of finite projective $\Lambda_X$-modules: at every coefficient stage the local terms are actual direct summands of finite sums of the coefficient unit, with the localized and common-stage interpretations of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Then $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ is perfect on the coefficient site of $X$ in that same sense, and the evaluation $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee\to\Lambda_X$ is defined.

proof.text: Choose the local bounded models required by [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], allowing their bounds to depend on the covering object. At finite and completed integral coefficients, exact restriction and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] reduce the dual to the ringed slice. Refine the finitely many term covers to obtain degreewise finite-free retractions. Apply [lem-sfb-split-perfect-dual-tor-window]: the ordinary signed Hom dual represents the derived dual, is supported in $[-b,-a]$, and has finite-free-retract terms. These are the required local perfect models.

source.place: Assembly of the explicitly cited local-model, finite-tail and coefficient-transport statements; original proof steps 1–3

proof.text: For rational coefficients, [lem-sf-coefficient-dual-model-transport] identifies the restricted dual with the localized ringed-slice dual. Start with the bounded localized complex in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Apply [lem-sf-localized-signed-dual-presentation] with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$ and $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}|_U$: its lifting clause gives an actual bounded module complex $P$ with the same rational retract terms. It then gives the signed bounded dual $D$ and the invertible single-term comparisons to a fixed K-injective Hom model.

source.place: Assembly of the explicitly cited local-model, finite-tail and coefficient-transport statements; original proof steps 4–6

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-localized-bounded-hom-comparison] to that bounded $P$ and $j:R[0]\to I$. The single-term hypotheses are supplied by the preceding step. Thus the actual postcomposition map $Q_t(D)\to Q_t\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,I)$ is invertible. The target represents the localized derived internal Hom by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The bounded terms already supplied for $D$ prove rational site-perfectness by [def-weil-site-perfect-complex].

source.place: Assembly of the explicitly cited local-model, finite-tail and coefficient-transport statements; original proof steps 7–9

proof.text: At algebraically closed coefficients choose the site-perfect finite-field representative supplied by [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Its rational dual has the models just obtained. [lem-sf-coefficient-dual-model-transport] carries these bounded models, finite sums, retractions and finite-tail comparisons through a common finite extension and identifies them with the common-stage dual. The same definition gives site-perfectness at this last stage.

source.place: Assembly of the explicitly cited local-model, finite-tail and coefficient-transport statements; original proof steps 10

proof.text:
Finally use the specified adjunction $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}-\dashv R\mathcal Hom_X(K,-)$ in [sk-def-sf-operations], clause (i). Its counit at the coefficient unit is an actual morphism
$$K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)\longrightarrow\Lambda_X.$$
Equivalently it is the transpose of the identity of $K^\vee$. This defines the evaluation in the statement at each coefficient stage, using that stage's tensor and unit. This last construction does not require a choice of the local models or a gluing of their evaluations.

split_report.summary: Q110 repairs the batch5 re-split return. Kept the statement and all import/blueprint/Lean metadata unchanged. Reused the existing finite/integral ringed-site model rather than duplicating it. Extracted three statement-only nodes: localized signed dual presentations (old 5–6), finite-tail Hom comparison (old 7–9), and restriction/coefficient-field model transport (old 4,10). report.md retains the full original proof and maps every argument to these tasks or an existing theorem. The assembly has fewer than 3000 characters. Final review also exposed the rational differential-lifting issue: the signed-presentation task now explicitly lifts bounded complexes of localized module sheaves to actual complexes, killing the finitely many torsion defects of successive numerators. No retraction itself is lifted.
